prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: Distributed Systems Glossary (language en).
Grid: 3 columns × 8 rows. Row headers: yes (first logical column identifies each row).
Per-column content facts (content px at 15px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "Term" · longest unbreakable word 99px · one-line width 152px
  col 2: header "Definition" · longest unbreakable word 108px · one-line width 1472px
  col 3: header "Example" · longest unbreakable word 83px · one-line width 814px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 360px (the dashed pink box = the reader's viewport). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 359px.
Fixed: content, font, 15px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

The image shows the table's content with every cell on one line, so you can read everything. Study it first.
1) Understand it: what is the table for, how will people read, scan and compare it, which columns play the same or similar role, which values must stay intact, which text may wrap naturally, and where existing row height could absorb wrapping.
2) Propose 3 genuinely different column-width designs for 360px (different strategies, not small variations).
Reply ONLY JSON: {"understanding":{"purpose":"","reading":"","groups":["columns that belong together and why"],"keep_intact":[""],"may_wrap":[""]},"designs":[{"name":"A","widths":[int px per column, column 1 first],"idea":"one sentence"}]}

log.raw: {"understanding":{"purpose":"Define distributed-systems terms and illustrate each with an example.","reading":"Readers scan the first column for a term, then read across its row to connect the definition with the example. Wrapped lines should remain easy to associate with their row.","groups":["Definition and Example are companion prose columns: one explains the term and the other makes it concrete.","Term is the row identifier and needs enough prominence to support scanning."],"keep_intact":["Individual words and technical identifiers, especially long terms and unbreakable words in the prose.","The association between each term, its definition and its example."],"may_wrap":["Multiword terms can wrap between words.","Definitions and examples can wrap naturally at word boundaries; longer cells can absorb additional lines in the other cells of the same row."]},"designs":[{"name":"A","widths":[120,135,104],"idea":"Protect the longest unbreakable word in every column while giving the definition the largest share of the width."},{"name":"B","widths":[95,155,109],"idea":"Give definitions more room and allow term labels to wrap more heavily, accepting that the longest term word may overflow or require breaking."},{"name":"C","widths":[110,120,129],"idea":"Give examples the most space for easier reading, accepting that the longest words in the term and definition columns may overflow or require breaking."}]}
